statement: Current literature treats the causes of Neanderthal extinction as multi-causal rather than settled on a single factor, with population size/genetic diversity, climate volatility (particularly during Marine Isotope Stage 3), competition and resource overlap with expanding Homo sapiens populations, interbreeding/absorption into the larger sapiens population, and inter-group social-network connectivity all treated as contributing mechanisms in recent (2021-2026) sources, with genuine disagreement over relative weighting and no field-wide consensus statement identified.
scholarly_disagreement: Relative weighting of demography/population structure versus climate versus competition versus interbreeding-absorption versus social-network connectivity; a 2021 paper frames demography as the primary driver, while 2025-2026 modeling work treats demography as necessary-but-not-sufficient, decisive mainly in combination with climate-driven connectivity loss.

sources.citation: Multiple 2024-2026 sources (EU-funded research summaries, Smithsonian science coverage) stating that climate stress or direct competition alone cannot explain the extinction.
2025 preprint modeling inter-band connectivity and climate jointly as shaping Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens dispersal.
"An emerging consensus in palaeoanthropology" (2021), arguing demography specifically was the main factor — one paper’s framing, not confirmed as field-wide.

interpretations.position: Demography (small, structured effective population size) was the primary driver

holders.name: Unnamed authors, "An emerging consensus in palaeoanthropology," Scientific Reports (2021) — author names not independently confirmed in this research pass

interpretations.strongest_case: Small, structured populations with reduced genetic diversity are demonstrably vulnerable to stochastic extinction independent of any single environmental trigger.

interpretations.position: Social/network connectivity, interacting with climate volatility, was decisive; demography alone is necessary but not sufficient

holders.name: Authors of 2025-2026 network-connectivity modeling studies (bioRxiv preprint and related coverage) — author names not independently confirmed in this research pass

interpretations.strongest_case: Modeling that incorporates inter-group connectivity alongside climate and demography better matches the observed regional and temporal pattern of Neanderthal disappearance than demography-only models.

notes: Author names for several of the most recent (2021, 2025, 2026) sources could not be independently confirmed in this research pass and are deliberately omitted rather than guessed — cite by publication/venue only until verified. A named attempt to attribute specific positions to Fred Smith or Katerina Harvati specifically failed verification and those names are not used here.
